title: Large-Scale Comparison of Metaheuristic Algorithms via Behavioral Verification of Large Language Model–Generated Codes
content: The performance and reproducibility of metaheuristic algorithms remain unresolved because prior studies have examined only limited subsets, as most algorithms are published as mathematical descriptions without source code. A large language model (LLM) was used to implement 393 published metaheuristic algorithms. The LLM-generated codes were verified by running it on two optimization problems with three seeds while an automated script checked for crashes and improvement. These reports were returned to the LLM as repair feedback. First drafts passed at a rate of 53.4%, which increased to 78.4% after eight rounds of feedback, while 32 algorithms failed identically across all runs. The common practice of using LLMs to review LLM-generated code was evaluated: two independent LLM reviewers approved 75% of broken codes, indicating that textual review provides no information about functional correctness. Fifty verified codes were compared to reference codes from an established library: 49 differed significantly in both directions, and only the most completely specified algorithm was equivalent. The 360 verified codes were compared on the Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC) 2017 and CEC 2022 benchmarks with 51 seeded runs. Classical Differential Evolution ranked second on CEC 2017 and first on CEC 2022, outperforming hundreds of more recent metaphor-based algorithms.
